sections.title: Segment Performance
sections.subtitle: Cardiac & Vascular, Medical Care Solutions, Blood & Cell Technologies, and (from FY2026) Organ Technologies

charts.title: Net Income vs Free Cash Flow vs Owner FCF
charts.annotation: Owner FCF, where shown, is the DCF's series after SBC, interest income and lease principal.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Terumo Corporation: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Terumo Corporation: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Terumo Corporation: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Terumo Corporation: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Terumo Corporation: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Terumo Corporation: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Terumo Corporation: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Terumo Corporation: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Terumo Corporation: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

segmentRevenue.title: Revenue by segment
segmentRevenue.content:
Terumo reports three core segments -- Cardiac & Vascular (catheters, stent grafts, TAVI and structural-heart devices), Medical Care Solutions (hospital consumables, syringes, blood-pressure monitors, diabetes care) and Blood & Cell Technologies (blood-bag systems, apheresis, cell therapy manufacturing) -- plus a new Organ Technologies segment from FY2026, built around the OrganOx organ-preservation platform acquired that year.

For Terumo: Cardiac & Vascular has grown fastest and now accounts for roughly 60% of group revenue, overtaking the more mature Medical Care Solutions segment -- the segment mix shift is a large part of the margin story, since Cardiac & Vascular also carries the highest segment margin. Organ Technologies starts tiny (¥8.0bn FY2026) relative to the group and is not yet a meaningful swing factor.

What to watch:

  • Cardiac & Vascular's share of total revenue rising further
  • Whether Medical Care Solutions stabilises or keeps losing relative share
  • Organ Technologies' growth trajectory post-acquisition, and whether it scales or stays a rounding error

segmentProfit.title: Operating profit by segment
segmentProfit.content:
Segment operating profit, reported on the same Cardiac & Vascular / Medical Care Solutions / Blood & Cell Technologies / Organ Technologies split as the revenue chart, before corporate costs and eliminations (so the four segments do not sum exactly to consolidated operating income).

For Terumo: segment margins differ materially -- Cardiac & Vascular typically runs the highest margin of the three legacy segments, so its rising revenue share is a tailwind for the group margin, not just a volume story. Blood & Cell Technologies profit has been more volatile (plasma/blood-collection demand cycles) than the other segments.

What to watch:

  • Which segment is driving group operating-income growth in a given year
  • Margin compression in Medical Care Solutions, the mature/commoditised segment
  • Organ Technologies' drag on group profit while it scales (a new segment is rarely profitable immediately)

adjustedOperatingProfit.title: Reported vs adjusted operating profit
adjustedOperatingProfit.content:
Operating income is the statutory IFRS line. Adjusted operating profit is management's own non-GAAP measure, which strips out items such as acquisition-related amortisation and one-off restructuring or integration costs (relevant given Terumo's string of bolt-on acquisitions, including OrganOx in FY2026).

For Terumo: the gap between the two lines widens in acquisition years as deal-related amortisation and integration costs are added back -- useful for comparing underlying trading performance across years, but it is management's own definition, not an audited figure.

What to watch:

  • The gap between reported and adjusted profit widening structurally rather than just in acquisition years
  • Whether adjusted profit growth is translating into reported operating-income growth over time

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Terumo Corporation: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
